felt: It was the darkness that got you. It was heavy darkness, greasy and compelling. It made walls round you, and shut you in so that you felt like you could not breathe.
I felt as if I had blundered into someone else's life by chance, discovered I wanted to stay, then blundered back into my own, without a clue, a hint, or a way of finishing the story.
Then he just stood there in front of me and I kept on staring at him. The only thing I could think of was turkey neck and turkey gizzards and I felt very depressed.
What in effect looks like clear and directed writing took much chaos and anxiety. I felt like I was losing my mind toward the end.

felled:
Fate slew him, but he did not drop;
She felled—he did not fall—
Impaled him on her fiercest stakes—
He neutralized them all.
She stung him, sapped his firm advance,
But, when her worst was done,
And he, unmoved, regarded her,
Acknowledged him a man.
Fate slew Him, but He did not drop (B)

Could Hope inspect her Basis
Her Craft were done –
Has a fictitious Charter
Or it has none –
Balked in the vastest instance
But to renew –
Felled but by one assassin –
Prosperity –
fell:
I took my power in my hand
And went against the world;
'Twas not so much as David had,
But I was twice as bold.
I aimed my pebble, but myself
Was all the one that fell.
Was it Goliath was too large,
Or only I too small?
I took my Power in my Hand (B)

The sea is fulfilled, and the Empire fell apart.
Lord, Portugal must yet fulfill itself!
It was in the shady groves of dictionaries that Jack fell in love.

Ten days after the war ended, my sister Laura drove a car off a bridge. The bridge was being repaired: she went right through the Danger sign. The car fell a hundred feet into the ravine, smashing through the treetops feathery with new leaves, then burst into flames and rolled down into the shallow creek at the bottom. Chunks of the bridge fell on top of it. Nothing much was left but charred smithereens.

Upon the gallows hung a wretch,
Too sullied for the hell
To which the law entitled him.
As nature’s curtain fell
The one who bore him tottered in,
For this was woman’s son.
"'Twas all I had," she stricken gasped;
Oh, what a livid boon!
Upon the gallows hung a wretch (B)

Not with a Club, the Heart is broken
Nor with a Stone –
A Whip so small you could not see it
I've known
To lash the Magic Creature
Till it fell,
Yet that Whip's Name
Too noble then to tell.
Magnanimous as Bird
By Boy descried –
Singing unto the Stone
Of which it died –
Shame need not crouch
In such an Earth as Ours –
Shame – stand erect –
The Universe is yours.
Not with a Club, the Heart is broken (J)

fellowship: As a reader, I want to claim fellowship with "good writing" without limits; to be able to say that Hurston is my sister and Baldwin is my brother, and so is Kafka my brother, and Nabokov, and Woolf my sister, and Eliot and Ozick. Like all readers, I want my limits to be drawn by my own sensibilities, not by my melanin count.
